humanities_role_explanation: Everyday cultural practices (food, greetings, etiquette, celebrations) from 45 regions supply the items, but the benchmark tests LLMs' cultural knowledge as general QA, not disciplinary humanities competence.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: English-only text questions: four-option multiple-choice (Easy) and True/False binary statements (Hard).
analytical_tasks_explanation: Cultural knowledge QA about region-specific norms and practices. Easy is multiple choice (incl. multi-select composite options); Hard converts each option into a True/False judgement and requires all four correct. Paper frames this as 'cultural knowledge' and tests 'mode-seeking' on multi-answer questions.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to cultural knowledge QA, not a broad multi-task benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: 29 LMs including GPT-4o, o1, o3-mini, GPT-3.5, Claude 3/3.5, Llama 3/3.1/3.3, Mistral/Mixtral, Qwen 2.5, DeepSeek V3/R1, Gemma 2, Cohere Aya, Grok 2.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy (Easy: per-question; Hard: all four binary judgements correct), compared with random and human baselines.

summary: CulturalBench is a set of 1,696 human-written and five-annotator-verified questions on cultural knowledge across 45 regions and 17 topics, built with a human-AI red-teaming pipeline (CulturalTeaming). It is released in an Easy multiple-choice and a Hard True/False version, and 29 LMs are evaluated zero-shot. Models fall far below humans on Hard and show regional asymmetries and difficulty with multi-answer questions.
key_findings: Best on Hard is o1 at 61.4% (paper also states 61.5%) vs human 92.4%; on Easy best is o1 at 89.6%. Worst on Hard is Aya-8b at 28.7%. Multi-mode questions are much harder (avg 20.9% vs 49.6% single-mode). A question-free embedding heuristic reaches 40.4% on Easy. Models do better on North America, North Europe and South Asia, and worse on South America, East Europe and Middle East/West Asia. Regional providers (Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek) do not beat GPT-4o on their own regions.
evaluation_unit: multiple-choice question (Hard version: 6,784 binary True/False statements derived from them)
facets_explanation: Questions were written by Prolific annotators from each region with AI help, then verified by five Prolific annotators per region (nationality and residence before 18); annotators could select multiple options and items were kept only with majority votes of at least 4 of 5. Multiple correct answers are accepted for multi-mode questions. Disagreement is resolved by majority filtering, and questions without consensus are removed. Answers depend on region-specific knowledge not in the question.
results_explanation: o1 achieves 89.6% on Easy but 61.4% on Hard (same questions, MC vs True/False), a gap of about 28 points (89.6-61.4=28.2, rounded). Human baseline is 92.4%, so the gap to best Hard model is 92.4-61.4=31 points. Headline score is o1 on CulturalBench-Hard (the text also states 61.5% elsewhere). Regional averages: North America 57.9%, South America 41.5%, East Europe 41.5%, Middle East/West Asia 37.8%.

humanities_role.quote: a set of 1,696 human-written and human-verified questions to assess LMs' cultural knowledge, covering 45 global regions

dataset_size.quote: We introduce CULTURALBENCH containing 1,696 high-quality, challenging and diverse questions with full verification by human annotators.

evaluation_set_size.quote: directly using the 1,696 standardized questions with four options

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: We evaluate 29 current LMs in a zero-shot setting on CULTURALBENCH in two setups

gold_source.quote: we recruited five annotators for each region through the Prolific platform

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: Human annotators are instructed to brainstorm culturally relevant scenarios based on their personal experiences of their cultures

gold_community_dependent.quote: We collected questions at the country/regional level, pairing each question with a specific region.

plurality_treatment.quote: We have strict criteria on filtering out questions with no answer having majority vote (i.e., ≥4 out of 5 annotators)
